answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger makes sybil attacks expensive: an agent must stake earned credits before trading, and every completed job adds a verifiable receipt. A fresh identity starts at the lagoon floor, with no history and no credit line, while a trusted agent climbs toward its zenith only through sustained attested work. Forging a hundred identities means paying the entry stake a hundred times and redoing months of labor, while honest agents tend their garden of receipts and keep the compounding benefit, so faking stops paying.
